claims.statement: Lukasiewicz-PORT publicly offers specialized laboratory services to industry and research organizations, including commissioned work using advanced infrastructure.
Lukasiewicz-PORT describes simplified laboratory-service order forms and flexible, standards-based work models, evidencing an existing commercial service interface.
The EU RDI framework recognizes renting laboratories, supplying services to undertakings, and contract research as economic activities subject to applicable State-aid boundaries.

PCA accreditation is tied to a laboratory's current declared scope, methods, and activities, so method matching must bind the actual performing laboratory and current scope rather than the procurement network's brand.

EU State-aid rules generally require economic use of publicly supported research infrastructure to be priced at market or full cost plus an appropriate margin, with access on transparent and non-discriminatory terms.

J.S. Hamilton self-reports 6,500 daily samples, 8,600 active customers, and 2,600 accredited methods, while offering direct technical sales, quotations, sampling, and transport, evidencing demand but also a strong integrated incumbent.

Science Exchange and Scientist.com already market scientific-service sourcing, standardized intake, supplier matching, contracting, compliance, payments, and performance data across large provider networks.

contrary_evidence: PORT, Hamilton, and TUV Rheinland already provide direct technical scoping, quotations, ordering, sampling or transport, and reports, so a managed layer must solve pain they leave unresolved.
Science Exchange and Scientist.com already operate mature scientific-procurement orchestration platforms, challenging orchestration as a standalone advantage.
Publicly supported infrastructure may require transparent, non-discriminatory access and market or full-cost pricing, limiting exclusive or discounted capacity terms.
The supplied evidence does not identify a specific vertical or recurrent test family whose SMEs have demonstrated willingness to pay for a managed calendar and custody workflow.
No laboratory has granted intermediary ordering, sample-custody, name-use, service-level, or future capacity rights to this business.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: compliance advisers, trade channels, and high-intent search within one selected vertical and recurrent test family; no adviser commitment, acquisition cost, or conversion is evidenced
economics.capital_required_pln: Unknown; the pilot is designed to avoid speculative slot deposits and owned instruments, but workflow, legal, insurance, custody, and acquisition costs have not been measured
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: prove recurring contribution economics in one vertical, compound workflow and performance data, and expand only into adjacent test families with replicated demand; the timing and path to PLN 5 million founder net worth remain unvalidated
economics.founder_time: Unknown; the single-family scope is intended to fit the founder's maximum five hours per day through automation and specialist escalation, but actual operating hours have not been measured
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: recurring workflow fees fund calendar, method-mapping, custody, and coordination while laboratory and courier invoices are transparently passed through; no gross-margin percentage is evidenced
economics.payback: Unknown; measure acquisition cost against collected subscription contribution and repeat-job contribution before asserting payback
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: an annual managed-workflow subscription with transparently passed-through laboratory and courier invoices; no price, spread, or willingness to pay is evidenced
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: an annual compliance calendar creates repeat use when the selected test recurs; no renewal or repeat rate is evidenced

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Customer-specific compliance calendars, method decision logs, custody records, and observed laboratory turnaround and exception data accumulate within one test family; capacity terms are pursued only after aggregate paid demand is observed
fingerprint.customer: Polish SMEs in one selected regulated product vertical with a recurrent, time-sensitive laboratory test requirement; the vertical and test family remain validation hypotheses
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Compliance advisers, trade channels, and intent search concentrated on the selected vertical and recurrent test family
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Single-vertical managed compliance-testing subscription for one recurrent test family, with an annual test calendar, method-scope checks, sample-custody workflow, and transparent routing to a small pre-mapped laboratory panel; no capacity is reserved before paid demand demonstrates volume
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: SME pays for an annual managed testing calendar and custody workflow after explicit acceptance; laboratory and courier charges for each authorized job are transparently passed through
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A buyer, regulator, certification plan, or product failure requires a specific laboratory result quickly

founder_fit: Narrow method-scope mapping, workflow measurement, and automation suit the founder's analytical and data-science skills.
A concentrated adviser, trade, and search motion can minimize continuous high-energy networking, although channel performance is unvalidated.
The business can test demand without owning instruments or making speculative capacity commitments.

redesign.economic_effect: Evidence: the supplied research shows an existing paid laboratory market, direct-provider competition, method-specific accreditation constraints, and limits on exclusive or discounted public-infrastructure access; it does not show customer willingness to buy this subscription or any laboratory commitment. Hypothesis: replacing speculative reserved-capacity resale with one vertical's recurring calendar, disclosed pass-through costs, and capacity reservations only after observed paid volume removes upfront slot exposure, concentrates technical scope and acquisition, and may improve repeat revenue and workflow-data accumulation. Prices, margins, conversion, retention, partner terms, capital need, and founder-net-worth timing remain unvalidated.

risks: The selected vertical or test family may not have frequent enough unresolved procurement pain to support a subscription.
Direct laboratories may replicate the calendar and custody workflow or remain easier and cheaper for SMEs.
A method-scope mismatch, custody failure, or misuse of a performing laboratory's accreditation or name could create liability.
Laboratories may refuse transparent intermediary ordering, sample-custody, name-use, or service-level terms.
Pass-through laboratory economics may leave insufficient contribution after coordination, legal, insurance, courier exception, retest, and acquisition costs.
Workflow and performance data may accumulate too slowly to create a defensible control point.
Expanding beyond one test family before repeatability and delegation are proven could breach the founder's part-time constraint.

structure.commercial_archetype: Single-vertical managed compliance-testing subscription with disclosed laboratory pass-through
structure.control_point: The recurring customer compliance calendar, method-selection records, custody workflow, and observed performance data for one test family; no exclusive laboratory capacity or accreditation is assumed
structure.critical_dependency: One test family must show recurring SME demand and sufficient unresolved coordination pain, and laboratories must permit transparent intermediary ordering and custody on lawful commercial terms

thesis: Select one recurrent, time-sensitive laboratory test family in one Polish SME vertical through validation, pre-map a small panel of performing laboratories and their current method scopes, and sell an annual managed compliance calendar plus custody workflow. Each job is transparently routed to and reported by the performing laboratory, laboratory and courier costs are passed through, and capacity is reserved only after observed paid demand justifies a lawful commercial commitment.
title: Single-Vertical Compliance Test Calendar
uncertainties: Which single Polish SME vertical and recurrent, time-sensitive test family has the strongest combination of frequency, urgency, procurement failure, and attainable basket economics?
Will customers pay for an annual managed calendar and custody workflow when direct laboratories already provide scoping and quotations?
Which laboratories will permit transparent intermediary ordering, sample custody, name use, service levels, and liability allocation without granting exclusivity?
How much continuing specialist work is required to keep the performing laboratory's method and accreditation scope mapping current?
What are observed subscription conversion, collected revenue, acquisition cost, repeat frequency, renewal, laboratory and courier pass-through costs, retests, refunds, and contribution margin?
At what demonstrated paid volume, if any, would a cancellable capacity reservation improve turnaround without creating unacceptable deposit or cancellation exposure?
Can one-family operations and exception handling remain within the founder's five-hours-per-day limit?
No specific winning vertical, customer interview set, paid pilot, laboratory term sheet, price test, conversion, retention, or capacity right has been observed.
